title: Evaluation of coherent isomorphisms in a Segal space
statement:
Use spaces, simplicial sets, nerves and coherent mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Put $\mathcal P_\Delta=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. For a simplicial set $K$, let $dK$ be the simplicial space with discrete values $K_n$. Let $W\in\mathcal P_\Delta$ be a Segal space, meaning that $W_n\to W_1\times_{W_0}\cdots\times_{W_0}W_1$ is an equivalence for every $n\geq2$. Its mapping space $W(x,y)$ is the homotopy fiber of $(d_1,d_0):W_1\to W_0^2$ over $(x,y)$. Let $hW$ have objects the points of $W_0$ and morphisms $\pi_0W(x,y)$, with composition induced by the Segal maps and identities by $s_0$. Let $W_{\mathrm{inv}}\subset W_1$ be the union of components consisting of arrows invertible in $hW$. Let $J$ be the ordinary category with two objects $0,1$ and one morphism between every ordered pair, and put $E=N(J)$. Evaluation at its edge $0\to1$ induces a natural equivalence of spaces over $W_0^2$
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P_\Delta}(dE,W)\xrightarrow{\simeq}W_{\mathrm{inv}}.$$
Consequently its homotopy fiber over $(x,y)$ is the union of invertible components of $W(x,y)$. No completeness condition on $W$ is assumed.
